rationale: All four of my round-5 asks are addressed at 8b3a5535, and the new F2 rule answers the lead's two questions the right way. Empirically, on this repository's main, all 37 tracked bead-targeted registrations have a reviewed_head_sha that is an ancestor of main (0 outside, 0 missing objects, no bead with more than one registration directory), so 'any outside-tip registration refuses' would have refused none of the beads that ever landed here. On a real-git fixture under the #239 topology (spec/S fast-forwarded onto main after a sibling PR merge; the first-parent scan sees only the PR merge, the topo scan sees each bead's own `Merge bead/<id>`): a one-round bead whose complete added a materialization commit D after the reviewed B has B in the tip's history (D != B, B an ancestor), and a fix-round bead re-panelled in place at F has F in history — and even if the `-r2` slug convention had kept the old directory, the superseded B1 is still in history because the fix is a child commit, not a rewrite. The only shape that refuses is a reviewed commit amended or rebased after the panel without a re-panel (B2 outside the tip, object still present), which is not the documented flow (ms-bead-fix makes a new commit) and whose exit is the dependent's evidenced override. A genuine #239 still recovers: for X and Y on the fixture F1 (one candidate each), F2 (in-tip), F3 (surviving tip equals the second parent) and F4 (content at the tip) all pass, so reattest accepts, writes the tuple, and the read-back identifies. The remaining items are MINOR completeness points about F2's inputs and should be consolidated, not block the gate.
concrete_changes_required: F2 visibility is per checkout, not per tree: `reviews/*/panel.json` is untracked during the spec's life, and untracked files exist only in the worktree where they were written, while `panel.Scan`'s roots come from the invoking checkout (`workspace.FindRoot(cwd)` and its spec dir). The same bead can therefore refuse F2 from the spec worktree (where ms-panel-run registered the panel) and pass from a bead worktree or a main checkout that has no `reviews/` dir. State this beside the visibility line, make the output name the roots actually scanned, and recommend running `reattest` and `ready-check` from the spec worktree; pin an AC-11 leg where the registration exists only in one of two checkouts.

F2 classification of a reviewed SHA whose object is absent locally (a round rebased away and then garbage-collected): `git merge-base --is-ancestor` errors on an unknown object, which F5 would report as an infrastructure error rather than `UnlandedReview`. Classify a well-formed SHA that does not resolve to a commit as outside-tip (it is not in the history, which is the only fact F2 needs), with the same refusal text and exit, and pin it (x-g).

F2 and an EMPTY `reviewed_head_sha`: today `reviewedHeadSHAForBead` skips an empty value as 'no datum'. Say whether F2 treats empty as absent (today's semantics) or as MALFORMED (fail closed); absent is the honest reading, because `panel create --target` sets the SHA in the same write as the round, so empty means no fan-out ever happened rather than a forged value.

Name the one normal-looking shape F2 refuses: a reviewed commit amended or rebased after the panel without a re-panel leaves the registration's SHA outside the tip while the bead's content landed. State that this is outside the documented flow (ms-bead-fix adds a commit; the guardrails forbid rewriting a reviewed branch), that the sanctioned exit is the dependent's `--allow-not-ready=MF-3 --evidence`, and that deleting the registration is deliberately NOT an offered recovery (it is the panel-edit reach the residual names). Add it as AC-11 (vii-a) so the refusal and its exit are pinned.

findings.title: Does 'any outside-tip registration refuses' refuse a normal bead? Measured: no
findings.detail: Live repository: over every tracked panel.json with a non-null bead_id (37 registrations), each reviewed_head_sha resolves to a commit and is an ancestor of main; no bead has more than one registration directory. Fixture (real git, #239 topology applied after three landings): bead X with one review round at B and a complete-time materialization commit D on top — registration B in the tip's history, second parent D ≠ B; bead Y with round 1 at B1, a fix commit F, in-place re-panel at F — F in history, and B1 in history too, so even the `-r2` convention would not refuse a fix round, because a fix is a child commit; bead Z with its reviewed commit amended after the panel and no re-panel — B2 outside the tip with the object still present, the one refusing shape, outside the documented flow. The primary scan over spec/S after the fast-forward sees only the PR merge; the topo scan sees `Merge bead/X`, `Merge bead/Y`, `Merge bead/Z` as fallback candidates (one per bead, F1 passes); surviving tips equal the second parents (F3); x1 and y2 are at the tip (F4). So a genuine #239 recovers for X and Y through reattest and the read-back, and Z refuses with the named exit.

findings.title: F2's input set is per checkout (untracked registrations), so its answer depends on where the verb runs
findings.detail: The spec states the visibility limit as 'registrations panel.Scan finds in the scanned roots: the repo root and the spec dir, in the current tree'. For untracked files the 'current tree' is the invoking worktree: this session's spec worktree has `?? .mindspec/specs/129-…/reviews/`, and a bead worktree or main checkout of the same repository does not. `readiness.EvaluateReadiness(root, …)` and `reviewedHeadSHAForBead(root, …)` take root from the invoking checkout, so F2 can refuse in one worktree and pass in another for the same bead and the same git history. Stating this (and naming the scanned roots in the output) keeps the determinism claim honest; OQ-10 already does the same for plan.md.

findings.title: Two F2 edge classifications are unstated: a pruned reviewed object, and an empty reviewed SHA
findings.detail: A rebased-away round whose commit was garbage-collected makes `merge-base --is-ancestor` fail on an unknown object; under F5 that is an infrastructure error, but the fact F2 needs (not in history) is established, and the refusal should be `UnlandedReview` with the same exit. An empty `reviewed_head_sha` is skipped as 'no datum' by today's `reviewedHeadSHAForBead`; F2's MALFORMED rule as written could be read to fail closed on it. Both are one-sentence decisions.

findings.title: Attacks that did not land
findings.detail: Anchors removed: a forged high-round registration can no longer neutralise anything, and an abandoned outside-tip registration refuses, with the dependent's override as the only offered exit — deleting the registration is correctly not a recovery. The #233 shape (second parent D descends from the reviewed B) passes F2 by ancestry without any tree-identity assumption. The read-back's no-op now requires a VALID audit (G3's (i-m)), so a malformed same-tuple audit is rewritten after F1–F5 rather than silently kept. The corroboration string's fallback provenance lets a JSONL inspector distinguish a fallback acceptance without re-running git. q9ea is rightly dropped from the fallback exits: restoring the branch satisfies only F3 and the fallback never identifies from a tip. PlanMapsBead and the spec/<S>-preferred plan source behave as specified; the divergence notice covers the stale-bead-worktree case I raised. No worktree was created; the scratch git fixture under r6/F3 is removed.
